title: clean: a sibling such as target.bak or target-old splits a build tree -- its nested directories are listed as skipped trees of their own, marked, and then removed with the parent
body:
FOUND 2026-09-23 by the critic-shell review of 0131's build, and DRIVEN by cc against a control in a copy of build0131, whose _clean_drop_nested is HEAD's, unchanged.

WHAT HAPPENS. _clean_drop_nested (lib/cmd/clean) keeps only the LAST root it printed, and drops a path only when it lies under that one. _clean_roots sorts the candidates before it, so a sibling whose name is the tree's name followed by a byte below `/` -- `target.bak`, `target-old`, `target-cc` -- sorts between `target` and `target/<child>`, and the child is then tested against the sibling instead of against `target`. Any cargo tree found by its markers can be that sibling, and any nested candidate can be the child: another session's `target/cc`, or a `--target` triple directory, which carries cargo's tag.

DRIVEN. A project with a Cargo.toml, `target/` holding cargo's tag, `.rustc_info.json` and `debug/.fingerprint`, and `target/cc`, a nested CARGO_TARGET_DIR holding the tag and `.rustc_info.json`. THE CONTROL, as it is: `clean rust --dry-run` lists `target/cc` under `target` as per-node, and skips nothing. With a copy of `target` at `target.bak`, the same run ALSO lists `target/cc` as a tree of its own, "1 build tree(s) with NO Cargo.toml beside them -- SKIPPED, not removed", and says it would mark it. `clean rust --force` then writes `.metadata_never_index` into `target/cc`, removes `target` and `target/cc` with it, and exits 0, having reported `target/cc` as skipped and not removed.

WHY IT MATTERS. The skipped list is what a person reads to learn what survives the run, and here it names a directory the run removes. The trigger is ordinary: a backup copy, or a per-session target dir kept beside `target/` rather than inside it.

WHAT A FIX MUST DO. Test a path against every root already kept, not only the last, so the answer does not depend on how the candidates sort. Sort in the C locale, as the rest of the file does, so the listing's order does not move with the locale either. An arm with the sibling present, and the control without it.

cc's, built with 0131 in build0131, since 0131's point 7 rewrites _clean_roots, and landed in one commit with it. It ships in 0.1.8 under hv's ruling.

## Resolution

Fixed at 81a8274, in 0131's commit. Ships in 0.1.8.

- WHAT CHANGED. _clean_drop_nested tests each path against every root it has kept, not only the last, and the sort is in the C locale, so target.bak or target-old sorting between target and target/cc no longer splits a tree. It takes and gives arrays (0141), with the same rule.
- RED FIRST AND MUTANTS. The sibling arm was red on the tree before the fix. Its second half, a tree found by its tag with a copy beside it, is the shape that still reaches the nesting test, since the walk does not look inside a tree found by name, and the mutant testing only the last root kept is killed by it.
- THE SUITE. As 0131's resolution.
